posts.label: The Clinic
posts.body: A private room in Oakville, no waiting area full of strangers, and nobody rushing the person before you.
posts.text: One client in the room at a time, in a private Oakville studio. No busy waiting room, no rushing the person ahead of you, no rushing you. Injections are done by a nurse practitioner and never delegated. See the room and the work on Instagram.

posts.source: IG: 5 Red Flags at a Med Spa
posts.label: How To Choose
posts.body: No consultation, bargain pricing, a provider who never says no. What to walk away from before you book.
posts.text: Five things to walk away from at a med spa: no consultation, bargain pricing, a provider who never says no, no named injector, and pressure to decide today. Your face is not the place to find out you picked wrong. The full list is on Instagram.

posts.source: IG: Behind the Scenes, The Prep
posts.label: Behind The Scenes
posts.body: New tray, sealed product opened in front of you, your face mapped while it moves. Zero shortcuts, every time.
posts.text: Every appointment starts the same way. A new tray, product opened sealed in front of you, and your face mapped while it moves, not while it sits still. The prep is the part nobody photographs. We photographed it, on Instagram.

posts.label: Real Result
posts.body: One syringe of lip filler, with her own lip shape kept exactly where it was.
posts.text: One syringe of lip filler, with her own lip shape kept exactly where it was. If it reads as good skin and a good night of sleep rather than work, that was the goal. Shared with client consent, individual results vary. More on Instagram.

posts.label: Common Question
posts.body: Forty five minutes for a first visit, most of it talking. The injecting itself is about ten.
posts.text: A first visit runs about 45 minutes and most of that is talking. Consultation, mapping your face in motion, and agreeing a plan and a price before anything is opened. The injecting itself takes roughly ten minutes. Questions welcome on Instagram.

posts.source: IG: Your First Visit, Step by Step
posts.label: Your First Visit
posts.body: A real consult, your face mapped in motion, a plan and a price agreed before anything is opened. Then ten minutes.
posts.text: Nervous about a first appointment? Here is the whole thing. A real consultation, your face mapped in motion, a written plan and price agreed before anything is opened, then about ten minutes of treatment. Step by step on Instagram.

posts.source: IG: Why I Do Not Post Prices
posts.label: The Question Everyone Asks
posts.body: Doses differ from face to face, so one flat price either overcharges you or under treats you. You get a written number at your consult.
posts.text: Why there is no price list. Doses differ from face to face, so a single flat price either overcharges you or under treats you. You get a written number at your consultation, before anything is opened. The honest version is on Instagram.

posts.body: A nurse practitioner, RN(EC), registered with the College of Nurses of Ontario. Never delegated, never rushed.
posts.text: Ask any clinic who is actually holding the needle. Here it is a nurse practitioner, RN(EC), registered with the College of Nurses of Ontario. Every appointment is injected by Cleo, never delegated to someone you have not met. Meet her on Instagram.

posts.body: Nurse practitioner and injector. Every appointment is injected by Cleo, never delegated, never rushed.
posts.text: Meet NP Cleo. Nurse practitioner and injector, and the person who will tell you no when the honest answer is no. Every appointment is injected by her, never delegated. The full introduction is on Instagram.

posts.source: IG: Welcome to the Treatment Room
posts.label: The Treatment Room
posts.body: One client in the room at a time. The door stays shut and the questions stay welcome.
posts.text: One client in the treatment room at a time. Nobody rushes the person before you, so nobody rushes you. The door stays shut and the questions stay welcome, however small they feel. Come see the room on Instagram.

posts.source: IG: This or That, Rested vs Frozen
posts.label: This Or That
posts.body: You should still frown, squint and smile. If people ask what you had done instead of whether you slept, the dose was wrong.
posts.text: Rested, not frozen. You should still frown, squint and smile afterwards. If people ask what you had done instead of whether you slept well, the dose was wrong. See the difference side by side on Instagram.

posts.label: Before You Book
posts.body: Your goals, your face in motion, what will work, what will not, and a written price. No obligation to book.
posts.text: A consultation is not a sales appointment. We go through your goals, map your face in motion, and talk about what will work, what will not, and what it costs, in writing. You can leave without booking anything. More on Instagram.

posts.source: IG: Preventative Botox, When to Start
posts.label: Preventative Botox
posts.body: It is not about your age. Make your strongest expression, relax, and see if the line stays. That one is setting in.
posts.text: When should you actually start preventative Botox? It is not about your age. Make your strongest expression, relax your face, and see if the line stays behind. That is the one setting in. The full explanation is on Instagram.

posts.label: Service Spotlight
posts.body: Small doses, started early, to stop a line becoming permanent. Prevention is easier than erasing.
posts.text: Preventative Botox, explained plainly. Small doses started before a line sets in, so it never becomes permanent. It is easier to stop a line than to erase one. Dosed to your muscle, never to a template. More on Instagram.

posts.label: Safety First
posts.body: Health Canada approved product, sealed and opened in front of you, injected by a nurse practitioner.
posts.text: The question people are too polite to ask. Product is Health Canada approved, opened sealed in front of you, and injected by a nurse practitioner registered with the College of Nurses of Ontario. Ask me anything on Instagram.

posts.source: IG: What 20 Units Actually Looks Like
posts.label: Unit Math
posts.body: Units measure dose, not strength. The number you need depends on your muscle, not on a menu.
posts.text: Unit math, finally explained. Units measure dose, not strength, and the number you need depends on how strong your muscle is, not on a price menu. That is why a flat per-area price rarely tells the truth. Breakdown on Instagram.

posts.label: Credentials
posts.body: Nurse practitioner, College of Nurses of Ontario. The person who will talk you out of it if it is wrong for you.
posts.text: Your injector is a nurse practitioner, RN(EC), registered with the College of Nurses of Ontario. Also the person who will talk you out of a treatment when it is not right for your face. Get to know her on Instagram.

posts.label: Worth Saying
posts.body: Ask your friend who started early. Softening a line before it sets is easier than chasing it later.
posts.text: Prevention beats erasing. Ask the friend who never seems to age. Softening a line before it sets into the skin takes less product, less money and less time than chasing it years later. More on Instagram.

posts.label: First Timers
posts.body: Most people booking their first appointment have questions they think sound silly. Bring all of them.
posts.text: Never had injectables before? Most first appointments start with a question the person thinks sounds silly. Bring all of them. You can book a consultation, ask everything, and leave without treatment. No pressure, ever. DM on Instagram.

posts.label: Compare
posts.body: Same family, different personalities. One spreads a little more, one kicks in a little faster.
posts.text: Botox or Dysport? Same family, different personalities. One spreads slightly more, one tends to kick in faster. Which suits you depends on the area and your muscle, not on which name you have heard of. Full comparison on Instagram.

posts.source: IG: Botox vs Dysport at a Glance
posts.label: At A Glance
posts.body: Onset, spread and longevity side by side, so you can ask a better question at your consult.
posts.text: Onset, spread and how long each one lasts, side by side. Not so you can pick for yourself, but so you can ask a sharper question at your consultation. The comparison card is on Instagram.

posts.label: Aftercare
posts.body: Stay upright, skip the gym, leave the area alone. Three rules, and they matter more than the rest.
posts.text: Aftercare, the short version. Stay upright for four hours, skip the gym for the rest of the day, and leave the treated area alone. Three rules that matter more than everything else you will read online. Full guide on Instagram.

posts.source: IG: Botox Aftercare, The First 48 Hours
posts.label: Aftercare
posts.body: What to do, what to skip, and what is completely normal. You got treated, now what?
posts.text: You got Botox. Now what? What to do, what to skip, and which small things are completely normal in the first 48 hours. Save it before your appointment, not after. The full guide is on Instagram.

posts.label: How We Plan
posts.body: Your face is mapped while it moves, because a muscle at rest tells you almost nothing.
posts.text: Every face gets its own map. Yours is drawn while it moves, because a muscle sitting still tells you almost nothing about where the product should go. That map is why two people never get the same dose. On Instagram.

posts.label: Honest Answer
posts.body: A quick pinch, a few seconds an area. Most people say it is easier than they had built up.
posts.text: Does it hurt? Honest answer, a quick pinch and a few seconds per area. The needle is very fine and most people say it was easier than the version they had built up in their head. No fluff, on Instagram.

posts.label: The Philosophy
posts.body: The goal is never a new face. It is the same face, on a better week, and nobody able to say why.
posts.text: The goal is never a new face. It is your face on a better week, with nobody able to say quite why. If the result announces itself, something went wrong. See what that looks like on Instagram.

posts.label: Honest Expectations
posts.body: It softens movement lines. It will not lift heavy skin, fill volume, or fix sun damage.
posts.text: Five things Botox cannot do. It softens lines made by movement. It will not lift heavy skin, replace lost volume, or undo sun damage. Knowing the limits is how you avoid paying for the wrong treatment. Full list on Instagram.

posts.label: Straight Talk
posts.body: If the line is there when your face is completely still, it needs something other than a neuromodulator.
posts.text: If a line is still there when your face is completely still, Botox is not the answer for it. That is a volume or a skin quality question, and it needs a different plan. Honest expectations, always. More on Instagram.

posts.label: Booking
posts.body: Message on Instagram and you get an answer from Cleo, not an auto reply or a call centre.
posts.text: Booking is a message, not a phone tree. Send a DM on Instagram and it is answered by Cleo herself, usually the same day. Tell me what is bothering you and I will tell you honestly whether I can help. We are at 3060 Preserve Dr, Oakville.

posts.label: The Standard
posts.body: You will not look done. You will look like you had a very good week of sleep.
posts.text: You will not look done. You will look like you slept properly for a week. That is the whole standard here, and it is why the dose is built around your face instead of a template. See it on Instagram.

posts.source: IG: Myth vs Truth, The Frozen Face
posts.label: Myth vs Truth
posts.body: Frozen is a dosing mistake, not an inevitable result. Movement is meant to stay.
posts.text: The frozen face is a dosing mistake, not what the treatment does. Done properly you keep your expressions and lose the deep etched lines. The classic fear, debunked on Instagram.

posts.label: Client Words
posts.body: That was the point. The best compliment is being asked whether you changed your skincare.
posts.text: Nobody guessed. That was the point. The compliment we are aiming for is whether you changed your skincare or got back from holiday, never what you had done. Client words on Instagram.

posts.label: Where We Are
posts.body: 3060 Preserve Dr, with clients travelling in from Burlington, Milton and Mississauga.
posts.text: Based at 3060 Preserve Dr in Oakville, with clients coming from Burlington, Milton and Mississauga. Private studio, free parking at the door, one appointment in the room at a time. Say hello on Instagram.

posts.label: Ask Better
posts.body: Lines from movement need one. Lost volume needs the other. Most people ask for the wrong one.
posts.text: Botox or filler? You might be asking for the wrong one. Lines made by movement need a neuromodulator. Hollowness and lost volume need filler. Booking the wrong one is the most common and most expensive mistake. Explained on Instagram.

posts.label: Which Is It
posts.body: Pull the skin gently taut. If the line disappears it is movement. If it stays it is volume.
posts.text: Here is the test. Gently pull the skin taut. If the line disappears it is a movement line. If it stays put, it is a volume question. Which one is your actual concern? More on Instagram.

posts.label: Before You Book
posts.body: Who injects me, what are your credentials, what product, what dose, and what happens if I am unhappy.
posts.text: Five questions worth asking any clinic, including this one. Who is injecting me, what are your credentials, which product, what dose, and what happens if I am not happy. A good clinic answers all five without flinching. More on Instagram.

posts.text: You asked, so here are the honest answers. The questions that land in my DMs every week, answered without the marketing gloss, including the ones clinics usually dodge. Read them on Instagram.

posts.text: The question people ask quietly, in private, almost every week. Here it is in public with a straight answer and nothing dressed up. Your questions are always welcome on Instagram.

posts.label: Included
posts.body: A follow up check at two weeks is part of the treatment, not an upsell. Small adjustments are free.
posts.text: Your two week follow up is part of the treatment, not an extra. Botox takes about fourteen days to settle, so that is when we look properly and make small adjustments if anything needs it. No charge for that visit. More on Instagram.

posts.source: IG: How Long Does Botox Really Last?
posts.label: The Timeline
posts.body: Three to four months for most people. Metabolism, dose and muscle strength all move that number.
posts.text: Three to four months for most people, and the honest reasons it varies. Your metabolism, the dose, how strong the muscle is, and how long you have been treating it. The month by month timeline is on Instagram.

posts.label: Week By Week
posts.body: Day three it starts. Two weeks it settles. Month three it softens. Month four you are due.
posts.text: Week by week, what to expect. Movement starts easing around day three, it fully settles at two weeks, softens through month three, and by month four you are due. Knowing the curve stops the day five panic. On Instagram.

posts.text: October is a month about lips. What one syringe actually does, the difference between natural and overdone, aftercare that matters, and real results shared with consent. Follow along on Instagram so you do not miss the start.
